author: William Allingham
title: Rhymes for the Young Folk
edition: Cassell and Company, Limited, London, Paris, New York and Melbourne, Smithsonian copy catalogued 1887 (Internet Archive Rhymesyoungfolk00Alli). Selected text fully collated line by line against its primary page images, using Gutenberg 46702 as transcription base without claiming its print exemplar is known. The second stanza of I Love You, Dear ends with the comma in the scan, correcting the period in Gutenberg. Plain-text conventions retained: straight quotation marks and apostrophes, double hyphens for em dashes, underscores for italics, capitals for small capitals; indentation normalized; illustrations and repeated musical setting excluded. The library text holds the whole book from the dedication and motto verse to “A RIDDLE”, taken from Gutenberg 46702 with the scan corrections declared here; only the poems used as nightly readings were collated with the scan, and the other poems follow Gutenberg 46702 as transcribed. Poem titles are headings; the title page, contents, list of illustrations, the pictorial “Introduction” page, illustrations, musical settings and the publisher’s catalogue are omitted. On 2026-11-18 the poems read by Kindergarten calendar readings, “The Fairies”, “The Elf Singing”, “The Fairy King”, “Robin Redbreast”, “The Cat and the Dog”, “A Swing Song” and “Tom Cricket” (blocks 3–8, 10–12, 14–17, 23–25, 51–54, 112–116 and 152–157), were collated word by word with the same scan in the same way (its Internet Archive OCR compared after whitespace normalisation, every difference decided on the page image); they match except that Tom Cricket’s “I'm too slim.'” closes with a single quotation mark in the scan, now adopted (the o and t of “potato” in that stanza are only partly inked), so no reading changed. Block 117, after “A Swing Song”, is the verse printed under the tune on page 57 rather than a stanza of the poem, and no reading includes it. A further collation on 2026-11-18, made the same way for Kindergarten calendar readings, of “Here and There”, “The Lepracaun”, “Down on the Shore” and “Riding” (blocks 56–74, 96–100, 123–125 and 144–150) found seven places where the scan differs from Gutenberg, all adopted (listed under acquisition), in poems no reading had used, so no existing reading changed; the first stanza and chorus of “Here and There” are printed only as the words under its tune on page 37, set in roman, and are kept as Gutenberg divides them into lines, without the tune’s syllable hyphens (“Lu-cy”, “play-mates”, “beech-nuts”).

rights.basis: This original English text was published in 1887, before 1931, and its US publication copyright term has expired by 2026. Only the historical poem text is reproduced; modern editorial material and illustrations are excluded.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg plain text (pg46702.txt from the aleph.pglaf.org mirror) with the PG header, footer, licence and transcriber’s note removed; [Illustration] placeholders (including the pictured musical settings), the title page, contents, list of illustrations, the “Introduction.” picture heading and the Cassell catalogue omitted. The dedication lines became one stanza; the italic motto verse one stanza; flush-left capitalised titles level-2 headings (“THE LEPRACAUN; OR, FAIRY SHOEMAKER.” joined from three lines); flush-left Roman part numbers level-3 headings; other flush-left lines (“(A JUVENILE CHORUS.)”, “(_Tyrol._)”, “[AD INFINITUM.]”) paragraphs; indented groups stanzas with leading indentation removed. One emendation from the scan, already declared for the nightly reading: the second stanza of “I LOVE YOU, DEAR.” ends “beside you, Dear,” with a comma where Gutenberg has a period. A second, from the 2026-11-18 collation for calendar readings: in “TOM CRICKET” (block 155) “I'm too slim.'” closes with the scan’s single quotation mark where Gutenberg has a double. Straight quotes, double-hyphen dashes, _underscore_ italics and =equals= bold kept as transcribed. Every Kindergarten night from this book was located block for block. Seven more, from the further 2026-11-18 collation: in “HERE AND THERE.” the first chorus (block 59) is roman as printed under the tune, not italic; Gerald’s, Johnny’s and Mary’s choruses (blocks 61, 69, 71) read “Happy and gay:” with the scan’s colon where Gutenberg has a semicolon; Henry’s stanza (block 64) has “round him.” with a full stop where Gutenberg has a comma; Bertha’s chorus (block 73) reads “singing” where Gutenberg has “sinking”; and in “THE LEPRACAUN” (block 100) “Leather apron--shoe” has the scan’s dash where Gutenberg has a hyphen.
